# Risk matrix

Adjust the wording to the company's own risk appetite when it has one. Financial bands are relative to the value at stake (deal, contract or annual revenue, whichever fits) and are a starting point, not a rule.

## Severity (impact if it happens)

| Level | Label | Typical meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Negligible | Handled in normal operations; no real financial, operational or reputational effect |
| 2 | Low | Small financial effect (under about 1% of the value at stake); minor disruption; no public attention |
| 3 | Moderate | Noticeable financial effect (about 1 to 5%); visible disruption; limited public attention possible |
| 4 | High | Substantial financial effect (about 5 to 25%); significant disruption; likely public attention; possible regulatory interest |
| 5 | Critical | Major financial effect (over about 25%); fundamental disruption; serious reputational harm; regulatory action likely; possible personal liability for officers |

## Likelihood (chance it happens in the review period)

| Level | Label | Typical meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Remote | Would need exceptional circumstances |
| 2 | Unlikely | Possible but not expected |
| 3 | Possible | Foreseeable triggers exist |
| 4 | Likely | Triggers are common in similar situations |
| 5 | Almost certain | Triggers are present or imminent |

## Score and level

Score equals severity times likelihood.

|  | Remote (1) | Unlikely (2) | Possible (3) | Likely (4) | Almost certain (5) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical (5) | 5 | 10 | 15 | 20 | 25 |
| High (4) | 4 | 8 | 12 | 16 | 20 |
| Moderate (3) | 3 | 6 | 9 | 12 | 15 |
| Low (2) | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8 | 10 |
| Negligible (1) | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |

| Score | Level | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 to 4 | Low | Accept or apply standard controls; record and review periodically |
| 5 to 9 | Medium | Mitigate; assign an owner; review monthly or when a trigger occurs |
| 10 to 15 | High | Escalate to senior leadership; written mitigation and contingency plan; consider outside counsel; review weekly or at milestones |
| 16 to 25 | Critical | Immediate escalation to leadership and outside counsel; response team; consider insurer notice and evidence preservation; review daily until reduced |

## Always route to counsel, whatever the score

- Lawsuits filed or threatened, and formal demand letters.
- Contact from a regulator, government agency or law enforcement.
- Possible criminal exposure.
- Breaches involving regulated personal data.
- Personal injury claims.
- Matters that may need board notice or public disclosure.

## Register fields

Risk id, date identified, description, category, severity, likelihood, score, level, owner (role), current controls, response, status (open, mitigated, accepted, closed), review date, trigger for re-rating, notes.
